about: Changes waiting for the operator's yes, run once from the phone: /approve lists them, /approve <id> shows one and a code, /approve <id> yes <code> runs it (powershell -File <script>, no arguments, detached through WMI). research/phone/actions/approvals.py says what may be listed. sha256 is of the script's text (CRLF -> LF, no BOM): an edited script is not run until this entry is updated.

items.title: Pin: drop the jump hedge AND 1.33x bet (trial) -- see pinsize, which keeps the hedge
items.description: Two edits to the pin bot's launcher (C:\kals-live-0925n\restart_bot.ps1). 1) The jump hedge (--hedge-jump 6) is switched off: the 10-30 read found 7 of its 8 hedges insured bets that won anyway and it caught none of the 3 real losses (about +$2-4 a day without it). 2) The bet goes from --bank-brake 4.00 to 3.00, about 1.33 times today's size (about +$2 a day on the 22 recorded days; the operator asked for caution, so not 1.5x). The script keeps a backup, checks the edited file still parses (else restores it and stops), then restarts pin through restart_bot.ps1, which waits until pin holds no open bet.
items.stop_rule: Back to --bank-brake 4.00 if any pin day during the trial is worse than -$100, or if the 11-10 read shows the extra contracts earning under 0c each (over +0.5c each -> consider 2.00).

items.title: FX taker: restart it on the 30-second window again
items.description: The FX code on the server is already back on the 30-second window (commit 42935f8), but the running FX taker still uses 45 seconds until it restarts. Today's 1:45 PM silver and platinum losses were both bought 44.9 seconds out, in the stretch added this morning: that stretch bought 96 and lost 2 (-$10.75), while 15-30 seconds bought 34 and lost 0 (+$3.32). The script waits for minutes 1-11 of a quarter hour, writes FX's stop file so it stands down with nothing open, waits for it to exit, removes the stop file and runs the server's keep-alive (KalsBoot), which starts FX again on the new code within a minute. FX misses at most one 15-minute round.
items.stop_rule: If FX loses again on the 30-second window before 11-03, the 11-03 read decides between keeping it, dropping platinum/silver, or pausing FX.

items.title: FX taker: one bank -- size every bet from both pots together
items.description: Restarts the FX taker on the one-bank code (it also carries the 30-second window, so it replaces fx30). From then on its bet size comes from ALL of FX's money together -- the currency pot (subaccount 4) plus the commodity pot (subaccount 5) plus its open bets -- at $20 of that bank per contract: today's ~$207 is 10 contracts, exactly what it bets now, so nothing changes today. It re-works the size only when it holds no bets: up at most +20% a step, down at once (after two cash reads agree). Its money caps move with the size (at 10 contracts: $70 in play per pool, -$25 day stop, -$10 stop line). NO MONEY MOVE IS NEEDED -- just approve. Why there are still two pots: Kalshi keeps cash per pool, the currency markets are paid from pool 0 and the commodities from pool 2, and a Kalshi subaccount lives in one pool (10-25: funding subaccount 5 in pool 0 was refused), so the phone cannot put the currency money into subaccount 5 today (/move 72 main sub5pool0 answers 'Kalshi does not list subaccount 5, weather pool'). If a pool-0 subaccount 5 is made later, the order is: 1) /move <sub 4's cash> sub4 main, then /move yes <code>; 2) /move <same amount> main sub5pool0, then /move yes <code>; FX then trades both pools from subaccount 5 by itself at its next restart. The script refuses unless the server has pulled this code and its self-test passes, waits for minutes 1-11 of a quarter hour, writes FX's stop file so it stands down with nothing open, waits for it to exit, removes the stop file and runs the keep-alive (KalsBoot), which starts FX again within a minute; FX misses at most one 15-minute round.
items.stop_rule: Back to the fixed 10 contracts (git revert of the one-bank commit, then a restart) if a resize ever lowers the size while the bank grew, or if FX loses more than $25 in a day at a size above 10 before 11-06.

items.title: Pin: 1.33x bet trial, KEEP the jump hedge (recommended over pin15)
items.description: One edit to the pin bot's launcher: the bet goes from --bank-brake 4.00 to 3.00, about 1.33 times today's size (about +$2 a day on the recorded days). The jump hedge stays ON: on pin's history (09-12 to 10-20) it would have cut the big fast losses (NEAR 10-03 -$87, ZEC 10-07 -$83, ZEC 10-18 -$33 to about -$1.50), worth +$76 to +$189 over those weeks, while its one live week (10-24 to 10-30) happened to have no fast loss and cost about $12.50. With a bigger bet, keeping insurance against the big fast losses is the cautious choice. The script keeps a backup, checks the edited file still parses (else restores it and stops), then restarts pin through restart_bot.ps1, which waits until pin holds no open bet. Choose this OR pin15, not both.
items.stop_rule: Back to --bank-brake 4.00 if any pin day during the trial is worse than -$100, or if the 11-10 read shows the extra contracts earning under 0c each.

items.title: Ladder: 82% money rail (bids ~118 -> ~138) + the moved-bid fix, one restart
items.description: Restarts the ladder once with two changes. 1) The money rail goes from 70% to 82% of its pot (--commit-frac 0.82, as asked on 10-31), so each 98c bid is about 138 contracts instead of 118 at today's $830 pot: about +$1.10-1.28 a day on the same fills, $98 more resting at once, worst single market about -$132 instead of -$113 (the ladder has never lost a market). 2) A fix: when the ladder moves a bid from 97.9c to 98c it used to count the old and the new bid together, refuse the new one for good and then cancel the old one, leaving that market with NO bid (11 times on 10-30, 21 on 10-29); now the new bid waits a moment for the old one's cancel and is placed. The rails are never exceeded. The script refuses unless the server has the new code and the ladder's self-test passes, edits boot_all's ladder line once (backup kept, parse checked), then restarts the ladder between closes (minutes 2-9 of a quarter hour) through the keep-alive; the ladder misses at most one close.
items.stop_rule: Back to 70% (remove --commit-frac 0.82 from boot_all and restart) if the ladder ever loses a market at the bigger size, or if its 7-day money per fill falls below the 70% rail's.

items.title: Pin: small 99c test -- buy 98-99c offers at a tenth of a bet, only in markets pin holds nothing in
items.description: Puts pin on a new build (C:\kals-live-0925p = today's build plus this one change) and restarts it once, when it holds no open bet. From then on, when sellers offer the winning side above pin's 98c limit but at 99c or less, in a market pin has not bought anything in yet, pin buys a TENTH of its normal bet there (about 28 contracts at today's size of 281), once per market. Every other safety check still applies; the one exception is the expected-value check, which at 99c refuses everything and would make the test measure nothing. One loss costs about -$28, one win makes about +$0.26, and there are about 78 such markets a day, so in 2-3 days we learn the real fill rate on winners vs losers (history 09-14 to 10-31: 2,967 such markets, 3 lost, +$3,679 if every order had filled; markets pin bought anyway were left out because those lost money). Scale up only if at least 60% of the winning band orders fill. It also logs the recent top price on every pin order (no trading change). It also fixes the keep-alive launcher, which still had the old 4.00 bet size: if pin had crashed, the keep-alive would have restarted it at the old smaller size. The script refuses unless the new build's own self-test passes with the full new settings, and keeps backups of both pin launchers (the one used by hand and the one the keep-alive uses), so nothing changes if any step fails.
items.stop_rule: Off again (copy the two .before-band99 launcher backups back and restart while flat) if band orders lose more than $60 in total, or if after 3 days the winning band orders fill under 50%.

items.title: Pin: restart once while flat on the same build (nothing edited)
items.description: Restarts the pin bot once on the build it already runs, nothing edited, through its own launcher (C:\kals-live-0925n\restart_bot.ps1). Why it exists: pin's two 1.5x boosts (the band boost on buys priced 95.5c to 98.1c and the last-10-seconds boost) used to switch themselves off for the rest of a run after a losing boosted leg, and only a restart put them back on. Since the 0925t build (11-04) pin runs with --boost-rail off, so that no longer happens; the phone's urgent 'PIN BAND BOOST OFF' or 'PIN LATE BOOST OFF' alert would still name this item if a trip record ever appeared. It is also the plain way to restart pin while flat (to load a launcher edit, or after a stuck run). The script refuses if no live pin is running (a dead pin is restarted by the keep-alive by itself) or if a restart is already under way. It waits until pin holds no open bet (pin is flat about 14 minutes of every 15; it gives up after 25 minutes and says so), then runs the launcher, which checks the code file, stops only the live pin process and starts it again on the same settings; pin is away for about 20 seconds. If pin buys again in the moment between the flat check and the restart, the launcher refuses and the script waits for flat again (3 tries). Every setting pin runs with today stays exactly as it is. Like every /approve item it runs once: after it has run, a new item has to be listed before the next trip can be undone this way.
items.stop_rule: Nothing to stop: a restart changes no setting. A restart also resets the run's own loss-abort budget (-$535) and its attempt counters; the day loss cap is unaffected.

items.title: Jump band: relaunch the live arm at 5 contracts after it ends its 14 days (about 11-13 3:13 AM ET)
items.description: Starts the jump band live bot again with the same command as its 10-30 launch: 5 contracts a buy, subaccount 3 (the $50 crypto pot in pool 2), 14 days, stop line -$25, log results\jumpband-live.jsonl. The running arm ends itself when its 14 days are up (about 11-13 3:13 AM ET) and nothing restarts it (it is not in the boot list); this does, once, when you say so. Its record to 11-03: 43 fills from 72 orders, 5 lost, +$14.22, +7.0c a contract, about $2.95 a day. The script refuses if a live or dry-run jump band bot is running (never two live bots on one account), if results\jumpband-live.stop exists (the bot's stop line or a human stood it down; delete that file by hand first if the relaunch is really wanted), or if the bot's own self-test fails on the server's code. The paper arm does not block it. It then launches the bot detached, waits 25 seconds and reads back the bot's first log lines. Still 5 contracts: the 10-contract step is a separate decision at the 11-13 read (bars: every live buy so far at +3c a contract or better, at most 15 lost per 100, no coin under -5c after 40 of its buys).
items.stop_rule: The bot stops itself at the -$25 stop line (it writes results\jumpband-live.stop and exits flat) and sends no new order for the rest of an ET day once that day is $15 down. Kill rule from 10-30: stop it if the first 150 live buys average under 0c a contract, or the first 200 under +3c, or any coin is under -5c after 40 of its own buys.
